summary: A point or direction in the world, as { x, y, z } in metres, where z is height. Arithmetic methods modify the vector and return it, so they chain, and you should call clone() first if you still need the original. Any object with x, y and z works where the API expects a Vector3.

x.summary: Along the world's x axis. You can assign to it.

y.summary: Along the world's y axis. You can assign to it.

z.summary: Height. You can assign to it.

up.summary: (0, 1, 0). Note that up in the game world is +Z, so this helper does not point up there.
up.example:
// The world's own up is +Z: lift a point by 2 m with a Vector3, not kcds.math.Vector3.up().
const above = player.position.clone().add(new kcds.math.Vector3(0, 0, 2));
up.exampleLua:
-- The world's own up is +Z: lift a point by 2 m with a Vector3, not kcds.math.Vector3.up().
local above = player.position:clone():add(kcds.math.Vector3.new(0, 0, 2))
up.exampleCs:
// The world's own up is +Z: lift a point by 2 m with a Vector3, not kcds.math.Vector3.up().
var above = player.Position.Clone().Add(new Vector3(0, 0, 2));

forward.summary: (0, 0, 1). Note that characters in the game world face +Y, so this helper does not match them.
forward.example: console.log(kcds.math.Vector3.forward()); // Vector3(0, 0, 1); the game world faces +Y
forward.exampleLua: print(kcds.math.Vector3.forward()) -- Vector3(0, 0, 1); the game world faces +Y
forward.exampleCs: Log.Info(Vector3.Forward()); // Vector3(0, 0, 1); the game world faces +Y

cross.summary: Makes this the cross product of itself and another vector.
cross.example: const normal = new kcds.math.Vector3(1, 0, 0).cross(new kcds.math.Vector3(0, 1, 0)); // Vector3(0, 0, 1)
cross.exampleCs: var normal = new Vector3(1, 0, 0).Cross(new Vector3(0, 1, 0)); // Vector3(0, 0, 1)

set.summary: Sets the components: set(x, y, z).

add.summary: Adds another vector to this one.
add.example:
const above = player.position.clone().add(new kcds.math.Vector3(0, 0, 2));
const distance = above.distance(npc.position);
add.exampleCs:
var above = player.Position.Clone().Add(new Vector3(0, 0, 2));
var distance = above.Distance(npc.Position);

sub.summary: Subtracts another vector from this one.
sub.example: const toTarget = target.position.clone().sub(player.position); // from the player to the target
sub.exampleLua: local toTarget = target.position:clone():sub(player.position) -- from the player to the target
sub.exampleCs: var toTarget = target.Position.Clone().Sub(player.Position); // from the player to the target

mul.summary: Multiplies every component by a number.
mul.example:
// 3 m ahead along a direction.
const ahead = player.position.clone().add(direction.clone().normalize().mul(3));
mul.exampleLua:
-- 3 m ahead along a direction.
local ahead = player.position:clone():add(direction:clone():normalize():mul(3))
mul.exampleCs:
// 3 m ahead along a direction.
var ahead = player.Position.Clone().Add(direction.Clone().Normalize().Mul(3));

div.summary: Divides every component by a number (not 0).
div.example: const middle = a.clone().add(b).div(2); // halfway between a and b
div.exampleLua: local middle = a:clone():add(b):div(2) -- halfway between a and b
div.exampleCs: var middle = a.Clone().Add(b).Div(2); // halfway between a and b

dot.summary: The dot product with another vector.
dot.exampleLua:
-- Is the target in front of the player? (the world faces +Y)
local forward = player.rotation:rotateVector(kcds.math.Vector3.new(0, 1, 0))
local inFront = forward:dot(target.position:clone():sub(player.position)) > 0

lengthSquared.summary: The length squared (cheaper when comparing distances).
lengthSquared.example:
// Comparing squared lengths avoids a square root.
const near = target.position.clone().sub(player.position).lengthSquared < 10 * 10;
lengthSquared.exampleLua:
-- Comparing squared lengths avoids a square root.
local near = target.position:clone():sub(player.position).lengthSquared < 10 * 10
lengthSquared.exampleCs:
// Comparing squared lengths avoids a square root.
var near = target.Position.Clone().Sub(player.Position).LengthSquared < 10 * 10;

normalize.summary: Scales this vector to length 1 (a zero vector stays zero).
normalize.example: const direction = new kcds.math.Vector3(0, 3, 4).normalize(); // about Vector3(0, 0.6, 0.8)
normalize.exampleCs: var direction = new Vector3(0, 3, 4).Normalize(); // about Vector3(0, 0.6, 0.8)

lerp.summary: Moves this vector towards a target: t = 0 stays, 1 reaches it.
lerp.example: const halfway = new kcds.math.Vector3(0, 0, 0).lerp(new kcds.math.Vector3(10, 20, 4), 0.5); // Vector3(5, 10, 2)
lerp.exampleCs: var halfway = new Vector3(0, 0, 0).Lerp(new Vector3(10, 20, 4), 0.5); // Vector3(5, 10, 2)

distance.exampleLua:
if player.position:distance(kcds.math.Vector3.new(1652.5, 2151.5, 37.5)) < 5 then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToPlayer(player, "You reached the well.")
end

clone.example: const start = player.position.clone(); // later changes to start leave the player's position alone
clone.exampleLua: local start = player.position:clone() -- later changes to start leave the player's position alone
clone.exampleCs: var start = player.Position.Clone(); // later changes to start leave the player's position alone

x.example: console.log(player.position.x); // metres along the world's x axis
x.exampleLua: print(player.position.x) -- metres along the world's x axis
x.exampleCs: Log.Info(player.Position.X); // metres along the world's x axis

y.example: console.log(player.position.y); // metres along the world's y axis
y.exampleLua: print(player.position.y) -- metres along the world's y axis
y.exampleCs: Log.Info(player.Position.Y); // metres along the world's y axis

z.example: if (player.position.z < 20) console.log('below 20 m: in the valley');
z.exampleLua:
if player.position.z < 20 then
  print("below 20 m: in the valley")
end
